brief:
The Israel lobby exercises outsized influence over American foreign policy despite public opposition to unconditional support for Israel, according to the Quincy Institute. Polling consistently shows majorities of Americans favor conditioning military aid on human rights compliance and supporting Palestinian statehood, yet Congress and the administration maintain near-total deference to Israeli government positions.

This disconnect between public preference and policy reflects the lobby's strategic deployment of campaign contributions, grassroots mobilization, and access to elected officials, the institute argues. The gap widens as younger Americans express less reflexive support for Israeli positions than older generations, creating potential long-term friction within the Democratic coalition.
title: Israel lobby shapes US Middle East policy against public opinion
